P. Subbalakshumma W/O Late P. ... vs The State Of Andhra
Pradesh Rep By Its ... on 12 November, 2024

Aphc010251052008
 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh
At Amaravati

] 
 (Special Original Jurisdiction)
 TUESDAY ,THE TWELFTH DAY OF NOVEMBER  TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY FOUR  PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE CHALLA GUNARANJAN  WRIT PETITION NO: 8071/2008 Between:
P. Subbalakshumma W/o Late P. Sambasivaiah ...PETITIONER  AND The State Of Andhra Pradesh Rep By Its District ...RESPONDENT(S)
and Others Counsel for the Petitioner:
 1. V R REDDY KOVVURI Counsel for the Respondent(S):
 1. GP FOR ASSIGNMENT  2. GP FOR REVENUE

The Court made the following:
ORDER:
The present writ petition is filed declaring the notification in reference No.G3/1948/07 dated 21.03.2008 issued by the 1st respondent as published in Eenadu daily dated 24.03.2008 proposing to resume the land admeasuring Ac.2.32 cents in Sy. No.1003/4 of Chinnachowk Village, Kadapa Mandal and District, which was initially assigned to the petitioner vide DKT No.169/78 dated 30.04.1968, purportedly for providing a house site to the beneficiaries under the Rajiv Swagruha Housing Scheme without following due process of law as illegal arbitrary and unconstitutional.
2. Heard Sri Talaseela Ravi Teja representing Sri V.R Reddy Kovvuri, learned counsel for the P. Subbalakshumma W/O Late P. ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh Rep By Its ... on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49975378/
1 petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondents.
3. This Court passed an interim order dated 15.04.2008 staying the impugned notification dated 21.03.2008.
4.

The petitioner submits that he was assigned an extent of Ac.2.32 cents in Sy. No.1003/4 of Chinnachowk Village, Kadapa Mandal and District, and he has been cultivating in the said land.
While so, when Joint Collector, Kadapa, proposed cancellation of assignment on the ground of violation of conditions of assignment, the petitioner has submitted an explanation, which resulted in the cancellation of assignment by order dated 17.10.1985, against which the petitioner filed revision before the State Government, which was allowed in his favour by order dated 16.04.1987 and since then, his name has been entered in the revenue records and he is in continuous possession and enjoyment of the subject land.
The petitioner further contends that he planted mango grafts in the year 2000 and also availed Agricultural loans from the Alankhanapalli Primary Agricultural Cooperative Society Limited, Kadapa.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. That being so, the petitioner has come to know that by way of impugned notification in reference No.G3/1948/07, dated 21.03.2008, the petitioner's land was resumed by the 1st respondent for the purpose of providing house sites for the beneficiaries under the Rajiv Swagruha Housing Scheme.
The said notification was published in Eenadu daily on 24.03.2008.

As per the notification, it was informed that though notices dated 18.06.2007 were issued by the 3rd respondent for resuming assignment granted in favour of assignees and as only 7 out of 30 persons have received notices and the remaining refused to receive the same, the notices have been affixed on the poles fixed over the land held by the assignees and upon considering the objection of those who have received notices the assignment made in favour of the 30 persons have been resumed and the land has been vested with the State Government vide proceedings dated 28.01.2008.

The notification further mentions that land has been taken possession from the assignees and respective assignees were called upon to appear before the 1st respondent along with the relevant title documents for claiming compensation thereof.

6. Therefore, the petitioner has assailed impugned notification contending that at the first instance,
she was never issued any notice much less notice dated 18.06.2007 proposing resumption of assignment and secondly, that never was 2nd notice affixed on the land on 28.06.2007 upon her alleged non receipt of the first notice, thirdly that the assignment cannot be resumed by the Tahsildar and it can only be done by the 2 nd respondent/RDO who should have issued notice and thereafter passed an order of resumption.

The counsel for the petitioner vehemently contends that respondents have not followed the proper procedure of issuing prior notice before passing orders of resumption, and the entire exercise is vitiated.

It is also contended that, assuming for the sake of argument that the petitioner's land was required for the purpose of providing house sites, the subject land should have been acquired by following the procedure contemplated under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act and that she be paid the compensation on par with the others those who part private lands and proposing to pay compensation as per G.O.Ms.NO.1307 Revenue (Assignment-I) Department, dated 23.12.1993, is contrary to the principles laid down by this Court in LAO- cum-Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella Division, Domalaguda, Hyderabad and others Vs.

2 Mekala Pandu and others1.

sentences.text: Therefore, he prays to set aside the impugned notification.

7. The Learned Assistant Government Pleader by referring to the counter filed by the respondents contends that initially the petitioner assignee was issued notice dated 18.06.2007, proposing resumption of land and was called upon to submit objection, if any with the 3rd respondent/Tahsildar on or before 30.06.2007.
As the petitioner refused to receive the notice, the same was affixed on the stick over the petitioner's land on 28.06.2007.
Despite following the said procedure, the 1 2004 (2) ALD 451 petitioner has not submitted any objections on or before 30.06.2007.

Therefore, the Tahsildar submitted a proposal for resumption to RDO and later on,
RDO once again issued notice to assignees proposing resumption of DKT Pattas on payment of ex-gratia
and as no objections were received from the assignees, the subject land was resumed subject to payment of ex-gratia.
Only thereafter, the 1st respondent/Collector issued the impugned notification dated 21.03.2008.

Therefore, he contends that the procedure adopted is fair and transparent and repeatedly multiple opportunities were given to the petitioner, but she failed to submit objections and availed the opportunity and as the respondents have rightly extended the benefit of ex-gratia, the interest of the petitioner has been sufficiently safeguarded.
It is also contended that besides the value of the land, they have also prepared estimates of the value of plantations and structures.
However, as there was no claim from the petitioner, payment of ex-gratia has not been made and therefore, he prays to dismiss the writ petition.
8. Perused the record and considered the rival submission.
This Court has gone through respective pleadings in the writ petition and as well as counter filed by the respondents.

It is apparent from the counter of the respondents that though initially the petitioner along with other assignees was sought to be served with a notice dated 18.06.2007 issued by the 3rd respondent/Tahsildar, it does not disclose the mode of service and the person on whom the present notice was served and even copy of the notice has not been produced along with the counter.

Further, the counter also states that the service of notice was attempted 2nd time by way of affixing on stick over the land on 28.06.2007,
however except for the assertion there is no other supporting material placed before this Court to believe the same.

When the last date of receiving objection is fixed on 30.06.2007, it is uncomprehendable why 2nd notice was stated to be served on 28.06.2007 leaving only 2 days time for submitting objections, even if any.

Though the counter also tried to mention that after the 3rd respondent/Tahsildar had collated the proposal for resumption of assignment and forwarded the same to the 2nd respondent/RDO who in- turn has issued notice once again proposing resumption of the assignment against the payment of ex-gratia, the date of such notice or copy of such notice is neither mentioned nor placed, conspicuously not forming part of the counter.

The relevant part of the counter dealing with the same read as under :
"On receipt proposals from the Tahsildar, Kadapa with his Ref:
B/750/07, dated: 18.06.2007.

The Revenue Divisional Officer, Kadapa notices were issued again to all the assignees including the petitioner in question objections within if any against resumption of the DKT assigned land on payment of exgratia as per G.O.Ms. No. 1307 Revenue (Assn-I) Department dt:23.12.93 in his ref:A/15/2008.
P. Subbalakshumma W/O

entities.text: Late P. ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since no objections were received from any of the assignees within the stipulated period the DKT lands in Sy. Nos. 404/28, 407/2B etc., to an extent of 56.81 acres was resumed to Government subject to payment of exgratia as per G.O.Ms. No: 1307 Revenue (Assign-IV) Dept., dated:23.12.1993."

9. Apparently, based on the proposals of the 3rd respondent/MRO, the 2nd respondent/RDO even without issuing any notice or providing opportunity, decided to resume the petitioner's land vide order dated 28.01.2008, which never saw light of the day.
Based on the above decision, the 1st respondent issued the impugned notification.
This Court finds that respondents have miserably failed to issue any notice or provide an opportunity to the petitioner before resuming the assignment made in her favour.

Even, if the said land were to be utilised for public purposes, it is apparent that respondents have clearly breached the required procedure, not once but twice, both by the 3rd respondent before sending a proposal to the 2nd respondent and even by the 2nd respondent before resuming assignment.
Therefore, the entire process of resumption is vitiated for violation of principles of natural justice and that assignment made in favour of the petitioner cannot be resumed unilaterally.
It is trite law that if the party is deprived of the right to property, the least required is to follow due process of law and compensate accordingly.

10. Accordingly, the present writ petition is allowed declaring the action of the 2nd respondent in resuming the land of the petitioner and also the notification in reference No.G3/1948/07 dated 21.03.2008 issued by the 1st respondent as illegal, arbitrary, violation of principles of natural justice and unconstitutional.
Hence, the same is set aside.
It is needless to say that the relief granted above is confined only to the petitioner alone.
There shall be no order to as costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
